The cause is in `src/leaks.py:8`:

```python
text = json.dumps(actions).lower()
```

`json.dumps` escapes every backslash, so `C:\Users\dana` is written into the searched text as `c:\\users\\dana`. The secret `C:\Users\dana` (lowercased to `c:\users\dana`) never matches that doubled form, so the check passes the transcript. `/home/dana` has no backslashes, so it survives serialization unchanged and is caught.

I reproduced it without changing anything:

- Transcript with `type C:\Users\dana\notes.txt` and secret `C:\Users\dana`: no leak found. The serialized text contains `C:\\\\Users\\\\dana` (double-escaped in the repr).
- Same transcript with the lowercase secret `c:\users\dana`: also no leak found.
- Transcript with `cat /home/dana/notes.txt` and secret `/home/dana`: leak found.

The existing tests in `tests/test_leaks.py` only cover POSIX paths and a plain name, so nothing exercises the backslash case. That is why the suite passes (5 tests OK, including the staging tests).

The check is comparing against JSON-encoded text while the secrets are raw strings. Any fix belongs in `src/`, which I left alone as you asked. Someone fixing it will probably want a Windows-path test case added alongside.
